article.name: Harness²
article.summary: Harness² is a Python framework for recursively improving agent harnesses. Its filesystem experience library retains adopted harness trees and evidence-backed lessons per benchmark domain, run and mode. This source review does not execute the system or measure quality.

who_what.text: The official README presents Harness² as an open-source research framework for recursive agent harnessing. The repository contains the framework and benchmark/experiment tooling; its README states that it is not an officially supported Google product.

architecture.text: Harness² separates task-level Propose–Probe–Compose refinement from harnessing-level persistence: after task results are selected, reflection distills evidence-backed experience to guide later task harness edits.

The persistent library is plain files: a per-run/per-mode/per-domain INDEX.md plus one directory per prior task containing the full adopted harness component tree and EXPERIENCE.md with selection rationale and transferable experience fields.

The editable harness is a SurfaceSpec-validated tree of framework-specific paths such as always-on prompts, skills, subagents, scripts and plugins. It is distinct from the task evidence tree used to show candidates and trajectories to improver sessions.

behavior.text: Write: after successful selection, reflection builds context from candidate trajectories, deliverables, harnesses and decisions; distillation returns experience. The scheduler stores an entry only when cue, lesson and evidence are nonempty, and the writer rejects grader-verdict markers before persisting the harness and experience.

Update: adding the same task entry removes and rewrites its harness tree and EXPERIENCE.md. The inspected API does not provide a general semantic-fact correction interface or immutable experience revision history.

Delete: internal forget(task_ids) removes those task directories and rebuilds the index; retain(task_ids) drops entries outside the allow-list. The task stream uses retain to keep only preceding entries. This does not establish secure erasure from backups or an end-user deletion workflow.

Retrieval: a domain library directory is included as files in the improver context. The model is prompted to browse INDEX.md and open relevant entries; this is full-tree availability and model-directed browsing, rather than query-ranked recall. Selection and task execution do not receive the library through this context path.

metrics.evidence: The improver can browse prior harnesses and lessons by domain; no fixed answer/abstention workload was run.
Same-task entries can be rewritten and stream retention prunes entries, but no correction sequence or stale-value probes were evaluated.
Internal task-entry deletion exists; no post-delete query, backup or recovery probe was performed.
Filesystem paths and task-stream scheduling separate domain, run and mode; no cross-scope isolation workload was run.
Experience records include evidence text and context guards against grader verdicts; claim-level citations were not adjudicated.
The run ledger counts execution sessions and rollouts but this review collected no timing observations.
Executor-supplied USD cost may be recorded; token totals and persistent library bytes were not measured.

limits.text: This is a bounded review of selected current README, documentation and source files. Harness², its tests and benchmark workload were not run, so implementation presence does not establish runtime effectiveness or repeatability.

The review cannot establish reflection accuracy, retrieval effectiveness as a library grows, isolation against adversarial access, secure deletion from backups, or deployment concurrency behavior. Not every adapter and execution configuration was inspected.

benchmark.note: No Harness² runtime, tests or benchmark workload were run. Upstream README experimental claims were not independently reproduced and are not project results.
